name: neurram
display_name: NeuRRAM (130 nm RRAM CIM, Wan 2022): 48 cores of 256 x 256

faithfulness.note: The chip's MVM is analog (conductance relaxation and IR drop, wan2021edge p.5, p.9): its error is not modeled, and a deployment on the bundle runs the toolchain's exact integer value law on NeuRRAM's geometry, permissions and physics.

notes: allow_coalescing and allow_neuron_splitting are true: "If the height or the width of a matrix exceed the RRAM array size of a single CIM core (256×256), we split the matrix into multiple smaller conductance matrices, each with maximum height and width of 256." (wan2021edge, Methods 'Weight mapping strategy onto multiple CIM cores', p.14), and "We therefore split them vertically into multiple segments, and map the segments either onto different cores that are accessed in parallel, or onto different columns within a core that are accessed sequentially." (wan2021edge, Methods, p.13). The bundle binds activation_bits 4, the input width of the profile's operating point: wan2022a Extended Data Table 1 prints its 16 TOPS/W and 3.9 us at 4-bit inputs (the chip runs MVM with 1- to 6-bit inputs, wan2021edge p.4); a run at another width declares it through target_overrides with a note. The cores are written one cell at a time: "In the weight-programming mode, individual RRAM cells are selected for read and write." (wan2022a, Methods, PDF p.10), so core_fields write_granularity cell and write_units_in_parallel 1. This bundle is the physics form of the neurram_like geometry, which it bundles once. [U-C4] The geometry counts RRAM cells and a signed weight takes two of them, so core_fields cells_per_weight 2 with weight_cell_rows 2 (the pair on adjacent rows of one column): "Each neural-network weight is encoded by the differential conductance between two RRAM cells on adjacent rows along the same column. The first RRAM cell encodes positive weight, and is programmed to a low conductance state (gmin) if the weight is negative; the second cell encodes negative weight, and is programmed to gmin if the weight is positive." (wan2022a, Methods 'RRAM write–verify programming and conductance relaxation', PDF p.10); the code release maps every layer so (weight_mapping: 'G = np.zeros([W.shape[0]*2, W.shape[1]])', 'G[0::2, :] = (W>0) * W * scale', 'G[1::2, :] = -((W<0) * W) * scale', python/nn_layers.py:33-37, the 'sign' scheme every notebook uses; Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.6558399); and the paper maps a 256 x 256 matrix onto two cores: "we generate a 256 × 256 random weight matrix with Gaussian distribution, split it into 2 segments, each with dimension 128 × 256, and program the two segments to two cores using the differential-row weight mapping" (Methods, PDF p.14). Each core therefore holds 128 x 256 weights (the bundle's cores, derived from the geometry's 256 x 256 cells), and a weight write writes, wears and is priced for both of its cells; the chip's cells, rows and columns stay 256 x 256 per core.
